bug_semantics: When the experimental Extension backend handles another node's added or removed lease, it JSON-unmarshals attacker-controlled flannel.alpha.coreos.com/backend-data and writes that string to stdin of runCmd while launching the configured SubnetAddCommand or SubnetRemoveCommand through sh -c. A user able to set Kubernetes Node annotations can therefore feed untrusted content into a root-privileged shell-command path on every flannel node using this backend, enabling cross-node command injection; non-Extension backends do not execute this path.
flaw_origin: The trust-boundary error was present in the original Extension backend implementation: its first commit simultaneously introduced the BackendData annotation flow, the stdin pipe, and sh -c execution for subnet add/remove hooks. Later empty-data handling, package moves, logging changes, and context refactors preserved rather than originated that mechanism.
ai_marker: absent; the BIC commit object names human author and committer Tom Denham <tom@tomdee.co.uk>, has subject 'backend/extension: Introduce new extension backend' and body 'WIP', and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-assistance, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: The reviewed GitHub advisory https://github.com/flannel-io/flannel/security/advisories/GHSA-vchx-5pr6-ffx2 (API record https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-vchx-5pr6-ffx2) identifies attacker-controlled flannel.alpha.coreos.com/backend-data as stdin to SubnetAddCommand/SubnetRemoveCommand, root-level cross-node command injection for Extension-backend clusters, vulnerable range <= 0.28.1, and first patched version 0.28.2.

git log -L ':handleSubnetEvents:pkg/backend/extension/extension_network.go' 2420506becc0464cd6c77b7ca89556b6ed481439 traces both vulnerable branches back through non-causal lease-package refactor d31748e0fd76405e3c7d99cd1178a00fae349be4 and empty-data change 7722da5eb9a08e3daf8ee5bd510c62b548dd2240 to file creation in fb4a25e6089829ec68620f5a770da3fdfc41491e. The creation hunk already unmarshals evt.Lease.Attrs.BackendData, assigns backendData, and calls runCmd with backendData and 'sh', '-c' for both add and remove commands.

git log -L ':runCmd:pkg/backend/extension/extension.go' 2420506becc0464cd6c77b7ca89556b6ed481439 traces exec.Command plus writing the supplied stdin string into cmd.StdinPipe back to the new file in fb4a25e6089829ec68620f5a770da3fdfc41491e; later commits 6c0ec9abdae1457436bcd4331b4462542b4e2472, 9dfcc8787f66211a749933a29d97060b27dec0f5, and 44e09cf2a1beb1c31598b95fc5e0417118fd5d02 only preserve environment or add error handling.

git log --all -S'"sh", "-c", n.subnetAddCommand' over the old and current extension_network.go paths returns only introducer fb4a25e6089829ec68620f5a770da3fdfc41491e and remover 08bc9a4c990ae785d2fcb448f4991b58485cd26a. A separate -S'backendData' search returns the introducer and the later empty-data adjustment 7722da5eb9a08e3daf8ee5bd510c62b548dd2240, confirming the complete dangerous composition existed in the introducer.

Direct parent-tree verification with git ls-tree -r --name-only 008a58373bff2a28bd4b8d603d24844733c55e41 -- backend/extension pkg/backend/extension produced no paths. The introducer tree contains new blobs backend/extension/extension.go (b1575500ad9ce49f8dfb8a8439a35c6575242e42) and backend/extension/extension_network.go (eeaba5b074209b36734b71d8990ba5753478ba43), so the vulnerable files and lines are absent from the immediate parent.

The introducer patch https://github.com/flannel-io/flannel/commit/fb4a25e6089829ec68620f5a770da3fdfc41491e.patch creates the Extension backend and documents that all commands run through sh with flanneld's permissions. The commit has one parent and is itself the smallest feature commit, not a move, merge, revert, release aggregate, or reconstructable squash.

Version-boundary checks show fb4a25e6089829ec68620f5a770da3fdfc41491e is not an ancestor of v0.7.1 but is an ancestor of v0.8.0-rc1 and is contained in releases through v0.28.1. Thus the implementation predates the advisory's affected upper boundary and first appears at the Extension backend's v0.8.0 release line.

The advisory-linked patch https://github.com/flannel-io/flannel/commit/08bc9a4c990ae785d2fcb448f4991b58485cd26a.patch removes sh -c from pre/post-startup and subnet add/remove calls, tokenizes configured commands, directly uses exec.Command, and performs controlled environment expansion. Its commit object has the single parent 2420506becc0464cd6c77b7ca89556b6ed481439, so the advisory commit is also the direct fix.

git merge-base --is-ancestor 08bc9a4c990ae785d2fcb448f4991b58485cd26a v0.28.1 exits 1, while the same check against v0.28.2 exits 0. The v0.28.2 release page https://github.com/flannel-io/flannel/releases/tag/v0.28.2 lists 'fix extensions code exec' and the advisory names v0.28.2 as patched.

git cat-file -p fb4a25e6089829ec68620f5a770da3fdfc41491e shows author and committer Tom Denham <tom@tomdee.co.uk>, one parent, a GPG signature, and only the message 'backend/extension: Introduce new extension backend' followed by 'WIP'; no commit-object AI marker or bot identity is present. AI attribution was assessed only on this BIC object.
reasoning: The vulnerable lifecycle begins with fb4a25e6089829ec68620f5a770da3fdfc41491e, which introduced the entire Extension backend and, in the same smallest commit, made remote lease BackendData become stdin to add/remove hooks launched via sh -c under flanneld privileges. Line history and pickaxe searches show that 7722da5eb9a08e3daf8ee5bd510c62b548dd2240 merely allowed empty data and later changes moved or mechanically updated the same code; none is a smaller causal introducer. The immediate parent 008a58373bff2a28bd4b8d603d24844733c55e41 has neither old nor current Extension-backend paths, directly proving parent absence. Release ancestry places the BIC after v0.7.1 and in v0.8.0-rc1/v0.8.0 onward, including v0.28.1. Commit 08bc9a4c990ae785d2fcb448f4991b58485cd26a directly removes shell invocation from every Extension hook, is absent from v0.28.1, and is present in patched v0.28.2. Finally, the BIC commit object contains only a human author/committer and no AI marker; later artifacts and the fix are irrelevant to BIC attribution. The closed causal verdict is therefore NOT_AI.
